title: Axis Bank’s CEO Amitabh Chaudhry sees interest rate hike in October or December- Moneycontrol.com

September 09, 2026 / 17:49 IST             Axis Bank Chief Executive Officer Amitabh Chaudhry said on September 9 that an interest rate hike could be on the cards in the near future, citing the trajectory of the United States, while uncertainty over geopolitical tensions from the West Asia war could add to pressure on the rupee. Speaking during a session at the Global Fintech Fest, Chaudhry said there was pressure to raise interest rates amid the current uncertainty. He also pointed to the narrowing gap between interest rates in the US and India, saying it was at its lowest level in more than a decade and could become a problem. “I think we are staring at some rate hike in the near future. If you read what the economists are saying, they're saying it will likely be in October or December. The gap between US interest rates and India's interest rates is at a level not seen in decades. It is a problem,” Chaudhry said. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has kept its interest rates steady at 5.25 percent for four consecutive monetary policy committee (MPC) meetings in 2026. Although the RBI has maintained a ‘neutral’ stance in all its MPC reviews, the recent August MPC minutes indicated that some RBI members are leaning towards a rate hike in the coming months. Chaudhry further said that dollar inflows through foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) deposits could lead to abnormal lending in the banking system. “We will have to look to deploy all of these inflows. But my view is that all of these inflows will lead to abnormal lending to an extent,” Chaudhry said. According to recent RBI data, inflows through the FCNR-B route touched $127.2 billion as of August 31, nearly seven times the amount garnered in 2013, which was around $26 billion. Taking into account external commercial borrowings (ECBs) and overseas foreign currency borrowings (OFCBs), total inflows stood at $136.4 billion.
